admission_apply.text: Fresh ink, and the word AGREED. You find no bargain it could be closing, and no sound it records.

native.admission_inspect: The ink looks newly dry, as if agreement were recent. You have no memory to match it.
apply_texts: AGREED looks written for you. That is absurd. The slip bears no name, not even yours.
Fresh ink, and the word AGREED. You find no bargain it could be closing, and no sound it records.
No new crease will take. AGREED stays small, finished, and unproven.
The ink is thinning. The conclusion is not. You still cannot say what was agreed.
The reverse is blank. Whatever was agreed left no terms, only this confident face.
The word feels rehearsed, worn smooth by repetition you cannot place. Only the slip is here.
With nothing to set against it, the word steadies you. The paper remains embarrassingly small.
You can name no second party. AGREED still reads as settled. The modesty of the scrap rebukes it.
You nearly sign on with the hand that wrote it. Nearly. Ink is not a witness.
You press the slip. AGREED does not yield. A sure account, and nothing beside it to trust.
You read it once more. The account does not grow. Your doubt does, by a very little.
inspect_texts: A narrow slip, clerk-neat: AGREED. No note of any sound heard, only that the matter is closed.
AGREED, in heavy strokes. The word seems to lean toward you, though the slip lies flat.
Creased now. The word survives the crease, which is more than the evidence does.
The face says AGREED. The back says nothing. Between them, a confidence with no contents.
The ink looks newly dry, as if agreement were recent. You have no memory to match it.
Thumb-sized paper. One sure word, AGREED, and no note of who, or of what was heard.
Worried smooth, it still reads AGREED. Repetition has not supplied a missing reason.
native.name: Assent Slip
